question.text: "Fundamental attributes" of a mutual fund scheme include all of the following EXCEPT:

answer.text: The name of the fund manager managing the scheme
The type/category of the mutual fund scheme
The investment objective of the scheme
The asset allocation pattern of the scheme

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p101-p102, fundamental attributes are the scheme type, investment objective (including asset allocation) and terms of issue. The fund manager's name is not listed as a fundamental attribute. p104 lists fund-manager name as a KIM item, not a fundamental attribute. The Trap: Candidates often assume the fund manager is a fundamental attribute because fund managers influence performance. However, a fund manager change does not engage the fundamental-attribute-change process. Note: Changes to fundamental attributes per p101-p102 trigger mandatory investor protection (written notice + load-free exit) — a key compliance distinction.
